title: Key Word Transformation: Inversion and Emphasis (Set 1)
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

items.sentence1: Hardly had the announcement been made when share prices began to fall.
items.sentence2Suffix: the announcement been made than share prices began to fall.
items.explanation: 'No sooner had + subject + past participle...than' is an inverted structure with the same meaning as 'hardly...when'.

items.sentence1: It was only by sheer luck that nobody was injured in the collapse.
items.sentence2Suffix: it not been for sheer luck, someone would have been injured in the collapse.
items.explanation: 'Had it not been for' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if it hadn't been for', emphasising that luck was the only reason nobody was hurt.

items.sentence1: The committee's decision was so controversial that it sparked nationwide protests.
items.sentence2Suffix: the controversy surrounding the committee's decision that it sparked nationwide protests.
items.explanation: 'Such was + noun + that' is an inverted structure equivalent to 'so...that', here used for emphasis.

items.sentence1: I'd prefer you not to mention this conversation to anyone.
items.explanation: 'Would sooner + subject + past tense' expresses a preference about someone else's action, like 'would rather'.

items.sentence1: They only found out the truth years later.
items.sentence2Suffix: that they found out the truth.
items.explanation: The cleft structure 'It wasn't until...that' emphasises how long it took for the truth to come out.

items.sentence1: Few people could have predicted how successful the campaign would become.
items.sentence2Suffix: anyone predict how successful the campaign would become.
items.explanation: 'Little did + subject + verb' is an inverted structure meaning that something was very unexpected.
